profile_text.body:
Arize AI describes itself as an agent observability, evaluation, and improvement platform. According to its site, teams use it to understand how AI agents and applications behave, measure quality with evaluations, monitor production performance, and improve prompts, models, and workflows. The company says the platform is built for chatbots, RAG systems, copilots, and agents, and that it integrates with more than 40 models, frameworks, and AI tools, naming OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon Bedrock, LangGraph, LangChain, LlamaIndex, CrewAI, OpenAI Agents SDK, and DSPy. The site also describes Alyx, which it characterizes as a tool for AI engineering that runs evals, debugs issues, and improves agents.

Its products include Arize Phoenix, which the company calls the leading open-source platform for AI observability and evaluation. Phoenix is built on the OpenInference and OpenTelemetry standards, can be run locally or self-hosted, and is used to trace AI applications, run evaluations, investigate failures, and improve quality. The company's own description of Phoenix covers self-hostable tracing, evals, RAG metrics, and embedding drift. Arize AX is described as the managed AI engineering platform built on the same open standards, adding managed infrastructure backed by a datastore the company calls adb, along with agent observability, online evals, and continual improvement workflows. Arize AI itself is described as offering ML observability, LLM tracing, an evaluation framework, and prompt monitoring.

The available record contains no litigation or MCP server information for the company.
